record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Glue the ultraviolet analysis of the Gross-Neveu model to its non-perturbative mass generation analysis at large N in order to obtain a constructive example of dimensional transmutation.

evidence.quote: Glue the ultraviolet analysis of the Gross-Neveu model [GK1][FMRS][DR1] with the non-perturbative mass generation of the same model [KMR] at large N, to obtain the first example of so called dimensional transmutation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional Euclidean Gross–Neveu model with N fermion components, defined (formally) by the action
S[ψ,ψ̄] = ∫ d²x [ ψ̄(x)(∂̸ + m₀)ψ(x) − (g/2N) (ψ̄(x)ψ(x))² ],
where ψ = (ψ_a)_{a=1,…,N} is a Dirac spinor field with N internal components, regularized with an ultraviolet cutoff Λ and renormalized in the standard manner. The model is asymptotically free and, at large N, is expected to dynamically generate a fermion mass m_dyn that is non-analytic in the coupling, of the form m_dyn ~ Λ exp(−1/(c g)) for a constant c > 0; this scale, traded for the dimensionless coupling g via the renormalization group, is the phenomenon of dimensional transmutation.

Existing rigorous constructive results provide:
(i) a non-perturbative ultraviolet analysis (including a Borel-summable expansion uniform in the UV cutoff) for the Gross–Neveu model at fixed N; and
(ii) a non-perturbative proof, at large but finite N, that the infrared (long-distance) regime exhibits mass generation, with two pure phases (selected by boundary conditions) and exponential decay of the two-point function.

Problem: Combine the ultraviolet construction at large N with the infrared mass-generation construction to produce a single rigorous mathematical construction of the two-dimensional Gross–Neveu model from arbitrarily small distances down to arbitrarily large distances, and prove that the resulting infinite-volume measure exhibits dimensional transmutation in the precise sense that the dynamically generated mass m_dyn is non-analytic in the renormalized coupling and satisfies the asymptotic relation m_dyn ~ Λ exp(−1/(c g)) (with c determined by the one-loop β-function) as the cutoff is removed. This would constitute the first fully constructive example of dimensional transmutation in a quantum field theory.
artifact.status_search_result: Existing constructive results treat the UV regime of the Gross–Neveu model (Gawedzki–Kupiainen; Feldman–Magnen–Rivasseau–Sénéor; Disertori–Rivasseau) and, separately, the large-N infrared mass generation (Kopper–Magnen–Rivasseau, Comm. Math. Phys. 169 (1995)). No published work appears to glue these two analyses into a single construction realizing dimensional transmutation; the problem is listed among open problems in constructive field theory and there is no evidence of a complete solution.

status_evidence.title: Mass generation in the large N Gross-Neveu-Model
status_evidence.snippet: Kopper, Magnen, Rivasseau prove infrared mass generation at large but finite N with UV cutoff in place.
status_evidence.claim: The large-N infrared analysis exists with a UV cutoff but is not joined to the UV construction.

status_evidence.title: Gross–Neveu model - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The bifermion condensate acquires a VEV and fermions become massive; the mass is not analytic in the coupling.
status_evidence.claim: Dimensional transmutation in Gross–Neveu is the expected non-perturbative phenomenon to be established constructively.
